mechanism_narrative: The observed two-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC, despite overall low levels, indicates a gradual return of consumer activity that will continue to lift mobility in this category over the next four weeks as people become more comfortable with public spaces.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below the average of the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: The observed strong and sustained increase in PARKS mobility, likely driven by improving weather conditions and seasonal patterns, indicates a shift towards outdoor activities that will spill over into increased general outdoor foot traffic for retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase, or decreases, despite PARKS mobility remaining high and increasing, indicating that seasonal outdoor activity does not translate to retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility, indicating a return to office-based work and commuting, will drive an increase in weekday retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks as commuters frequent local businesses and amenities.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing a sustained upward trend over the next four weeks, suggesting a decoupling of these activities.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained high level of RESIDENTIAL mobility, if it begins to decrease over the next week, will signal a shift in behavior towards spending less time at home and more time out, directly increasing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5.0 in the next week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains stagnant or decreases even if RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 5.0, indicating that reduced time at home does not translate to retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: The stabilization of GROCERY_PHARM mobility around -24% suggests that essential errands are being managed efficiently, potentially freeing up time and willingness for discretionary retail and recreation, leading to a slight increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above -25% for the next two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above -25%, indicating that essential activity stabilization does not translate to discretionary spending.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent upward trend in PARKS and RETAIL_REC indicates a growing public comfort with leisure activities outside the home, suggesting an accelerated recovery for retail and recreation over the next four weeks as people seek more entertainment options.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to show further improvement despite PARKS mobility continuing its upward trend, indicating a divergence in leisure activity types.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility fails to sustain its recent recovery and instead declines by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week, it will signal a slowdown in economic activity and reduced commuter footfall, leading to a decrease in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls by > 2 points week-on-week in the next 7 days
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases despite a significant week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES mobility, suggesting that retail activity is no longer tied to office presence.

mechanism_narrative: The observed two-week upward trend in TRANSIT mobility, indicating a gradual increase in public transport usage, will facilitate greater movement across the city and thus contribute to a modest increase in RETAIL_REC over the next one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next week despite TRANSIT mobility continuing its upward trend, indicating that increased transit usage is not translating to retail visits.
